definition_zh: 怀孕的；意味深长的；充满……的；孕育着……的
definition_en: carrying a baby inside the body, or full of meaning, feeling or possibility that has not yet shown itself
core_image: 一位妇人一手扶着腰，低头看向自己微微隆起的腹部
scene: 候诊室的长椅上，她把手放在小腹上，等护士叫号。The doctor told her she was pregnant with twins.
sceneCN: 这里 pregnant 是「怀孕的」（第 1 个义项：体内怀有胎儿）；句意为医生告诉她怀的是双胞胎。图中可辨识物件：长椅、候诊室、扶着腹部的手。

pos.zh: 怀孕的；意味深长的；充满……的；孕育着……的

derivatives.zh: 由 pregnant 换后缀 -cy 构成，义为「怀孕；孕期」
由前缀 im- 加拉丁词干 pregnant- 构成，义为「使怀孕；使充满」

senses.title: Carrying a child in the body
senses.definition: having a baby or other young growing inside the body
senses.definitionCN: 体内怀有胎儿或幼崽，正在发育
senses.example: She was pregnant with her second child.
senses.exampleCN: 她怀着第二个孩子。
senses.why: Latin praegnans joins prae-, before, with a root for being born, so the word pictures a child who is already there before it arrives.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praegnans 把表示「在前」的 prae- 与表示出生的词根合在一起，画面是孩子还没降生就已经在那里了。

senses.title: Heavy with meaning that is left unsaid
senses.definition: of a pause, look or remark, so full of meaning that everyone notices what is not said
senses.definitionCN: 指停顿、眼神或话语含义极满，旁人都察觉到没说出口的部分
senses.example: He let a pregnant pause hang in the air before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 他先让一阵意味深长的停顿悬在空中，然后才回答。
senses.why: A pause that seems to carry something not yet spoken borrows the image of a body holding a hidden life, so the silence looks ready to give birth to a word.
senses.whyCN: 一个仿佛藏着未说之语的停顿，借用了身体怀着一个隐秘生命的画面，于是沉默看上去随时会生出一句话。

senses.title: Full of something about to happen
senses.definition: holding a great deal of a quality or possibility that has not yet come out
senses.definitionCN: 含有大量尚未显现的性质或可能性
senses.example: The old harbour is pregnant with possibility.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧港口孕育着各种可能。
senses.why: If a body can hold a new life, then anything holding a future can be called pregnant with it, and the preposition with marks what is being carried inside.
senses.whyCN: 身体既然能怀着新生命，任何含着未来的事物也就能说成 pregnant with，介词 with 标出的正是里面所怀的东西。

senses.title: Fertile in invention, of a mind or remark
senses.definition: of a mind or a remark, full of ideas and quick to produce them
senses.definitionCN: 指头脑或言辞充满想法，随时能生出新东西
senses.example: Her pregnant wit turned a dull meeting into a debate.
senses.exampleCN: 她机敏的才智把一场沉闷的会议变成了辩论。
senses.why: The oldest figurative use praises a mind that is full and ready to give birth to ideas, a sense now mostly found in literary writing.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的比喻用法赞美一颗饱满、随时能生出想法的头脑，这层意思如今多见于文学性的文字。

intro.en: Pregnant comes from a Latin adjective that puts before together with a root for birth, and English took it through French with both the bodily and the figurative senses.
intro.cn: pregnant 出自一个把「在前」与「出生」词根合起来的拉丁形容词，英语经法语借入时同时带来了身体义与比喻义。

items.en: The root behind the Latin word for giving birth is usually reconstructed as gen-, meaning to beget; it is a reconstruction, not a word recorded in any text.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语中表示生育的词根可重构为 gen-，意为「生育」；这只是重构形式，并非任何文本里出现过的词。

items.en: Praegnans combined prae-, before, with that root, describing a woman whose child is already there before the birth.
items.cn: praegnans 由表示「在前」的 prae- 与上述词根合成，形容女子在分娩之前就已经怀着孩子。

items.en: The stem pregnant- supplied the cases used in running prose, and it is the shape that passed into French and then English.
items.cn: 词干 pregnant- 提供了行文中使用的各个格形式，也正是传入法语、再传入英语的形状。

items.en: Old French used the word for a woman with child and also for a remark heavy with meaning.
items.cn: 古法语既用这个词指怀着孩子的妇人，也用来形容含义沉重的话语。

items.en: English kept both branches, so a woman and a pause can be pregnant, and pregnant with extends the image to anything full of a future.
items.cn: 英语保留了两条分支，于是妇人与停顿都可以是 pregnant，而 pregnant with 把这一意象扩展到任何充满未来之物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the Latin stem for pregnancy; the near-meaning group gathers words for expecting a child and for meaning held back.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁「怀孕」词干上的形式；近义组收表示期待孩子与含义未尽之物的词。

entries.definition: The state or period of carrying a child in the body.
entries.definitionCN: 由 pregnant 转成的名词，指怀孕的状态或孕期。

entries.definition: To make someone pregnant, or to fill something through and through.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的动词，义为使怀孕，或使某物充满。

entries.definition: Relating to the period before birth; it only shares the prefix prae-, and its second element comes from a different Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: 产前的；只是前缀与目标词相近，后半部分来自另一个拉丁词，词源不同。

entries.definition: Waiting for a baby to be born, used of a mother or a family.
entries.definitionCN: 待产的；指母亲或家庭正等待孩子出生。

entries.definition: Carrying eggs or young, the technical word used in biology.
entries.definitionCN: 怀卵的；怀胎的，生物学使用的专业词。

entries.definition: Having a serious or important meaning that is easy to feel.
entries.definitionCN: 有意义的；含有严肃或重要意味的。

entries.definition: Hinting at something without saying it directly.
entries.definitionCN: 暗示的；不直说而让人想到某事的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of carrying a child, and its family keeps returning to hidden life, withheld meaning and stored possibility.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「怀着孩子」的形容词，同族词反复回到隐秘的生命、未尽的意思与储存的可能。

normal.en: Praegnans is prae- plus a birth root, so the word literally places the child before the birth.
normal.cn: praegnans 是 prae- 加表示出生的词根，字面上就是把孩子放在分娩之前。

normal.en: The stem pregnant- carries the meaning through French, and English added no new root of its own.
normal.cn: 词干 pregnant- 把含义一路带到法语，英语没有再添加自己的词根。

normal.en: Pregnant with is the fixed pattern for the figurative sense, as in pregnant with possibility.
normal.cn: pregnant with 是比喻义的固定结构，如 pregnant with possibility。

normal.en: Pregnancy replaces the adjective ending with -cy to name the state rather than the person.
normal.cn: pregnancy 用 -cy 替换形容词词尾，用来指状态而不是人。

normal.en: Impregnate adds im- and shifts the word to the act of filling, whether with a child or with a quality.
normal.cn: impregnate 加 im-，把词义转向「使充满」的动作，充入的可以是孩子，也可以是某种性质。

abstract.en: A pregnant pause and a pregnant woman share one picture: something is inside, alive, and not yet shown.
abstract.cn: 意味深长的停顿与怀孕的妇人共用一幅画面：里面有东西活着，但还没露面。

abstract.en: The word treats the future as something already carried rather than something still to come.
abstract.cn: 这个词把未来当成已经怀在身上的东西，而不是尚未到来的东西。

abstract.en: Anything described this way is under pressure to become something else, and that pressure is what the word really names.
abstract.cn: 凡被这样形容的事物，都绷着一股要变成别的东西的力，这个词命名的其实就是这股力。

examples.en: The doctor told her she was pregnant with twins.
examples.cn: 医生告诉她怀的是双胞胎。

examples.en: He let a pregnant pause hang in the air before answering.
examples.cn: 他先让一阵意味深长的停顿悬在空中，然后才回答。

examples.en: The old harbour is pregnant with possibility.
examples.cn: 这座旧港口孕育着各种可能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来个男童」——家里即将扑来一个小男童；pregnant 就是怀孕的。

root: 源自拉丁语 praegnans（怀孕的），由 prae-（在前）与表示出生的词根 gen- 构成，词干 pregnant- 经古法语进入英语；同族词有 pregnancy、impregnate。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hidden life carried inside; the senses divide into the bodily state, meaning held back, stored possibility, and an old praise of a fertile mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是怀在里面的隐秘生命；义项由此分出身体状态、未尽的意思、储存的可能，以及对丰沛头脑的旧式赞美。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a woman resting one hand on her rounded belly and looking down at it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位妇人一手扶着腰，低头看向自己微微隆起的腹部。

branches.en: a hand resting on a rounded belly
branches.cn: 一只手扶着隆起的腹部

branches.en: a speaker stopping mid-sentence while the room waits
branches.cn: 说话人停在半句，满屋等着

branches.en: a seed under soil that has not broken through
branches.cn: 土下尚未破土的种子

branches.en: a notebook crowded with half-finished ideas
branches.cn: 写满未完成想法的笔记本

branches.en: an unfinished sentence that promises more
branches.cn: 一句没说完却暗示更多的话

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix of place plus a root of birth, and English built its nouns and verbs on the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示位置的拉丁前缀加上表示出生的词根构成，英语又在同一词干上造出名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Pregnant goes back to Latin praegnans and its stem pregnant-, built from prae- and a root for birth; Latin also used gravida for a pregnant woman.
latinIntro.cn: pregnant 上溯拉丁语 praegnans 及其词干 pregnant-，由 prae- 与表示出生的词根构成；拉丁语另用 gravida 指孕妇。

items.meaning: the stem used in inflected cases
the state of carrying a child
to make pregnant or to fill throughout

definition_zh: 前提；前提假设；（复数）房屋及场地；法律文书开头陈述的事实；以……为前提预先提出
definition_en: a statement accepted as true and used as the basis of an argument, or (in the plural) a building and its land
core_image: 长桌的四条桌腿先稳稳立住，桌面上才摆得下一层层叠起的论证卡片
scene: 辩论开始前，主持人提醒双方先确认共同接受的基本判断，否则后面的推论都无处落脚。The whole argument rests on a premise that nobody has tested.
sceneCN: 这里指论证所依据的基本判断（第 1 个义项：作为论证基础的前提命题）；句意为整个论证都建立在一个无人检验过的前提上；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 前提；前提假设；（复数）房屋及场地
以……为前提预先提出（较少用）

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「房屋及场地；营业场所」
由动词加已然词尾构成，义为「以……为基础的」
逻辑学中的另一种拼写，义同「前提」
由「前提」与「基于」复合而成，义为「以前提为基础的」

senses.title: A proposition that supports an argument
senses.definition: a statement put forward as true so that a conclusion can be drawn from it
senses.definitionCN: 作为真实陈述提出、以便从中推出结论的命题
senses.example: The main premise of the essay is that prices reflect information.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章的主要前提是价格反映信息。
senses.why: The Latin word meant something sent before, and this sense places the statement ahead of the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词本义是「事先送出之物」，这一义项把它放在结论之前。

senses.title: An assumption taken without proof
senses.titleCN: 未加证明就接受的假设
senses.definition: a belief that a study or person accepts as true without testing it
senses.definitionCN: 研究或个人未经检验就当作真实的信念
senses.example: The model works only if its premise about human rationality holds.
senses.exampleCN: 只有当模型关于人类理性的假设成立时，它才有效。
senses.why: What is put before an argument is often simply granted, which is how a premise becomes an assumption.
senses.whyCN: 放在论证之前的东西常被直接认可，「前提」由此变成「假设」。

senses.title: The major premise of a syllogism
senses.definition: the general statement from which a syllogism begins, before the minor premise is applied
senses.definitionCN: 三段论起始的一般性陈述，在其后接上小前提
senses.example: The major premise says all mammals are warm-blooded.
senses.exampleCN: 大前提说所有哺乳动物都是温血的。
senses.why: Logic gave the word a fixed slot: the general claim sits first, and the specific case is placed under it.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学给这个词一个固定位置：一般性主张坐第一，具体事例被置于其下。

senses.title: The minor premise of a syllogism
senses.definition: the specific statement that brings a particular case under the general one
senses.definitionCN: 把具体事例归入一般陈述之下的特定陈述
senses.example: The minor premise states that this animal is a mammal.
senses.exampleCN: 小前提陈述这只动物是哺乳动物。
senses.why: The second slot in the syllogism is also called a premise, since both statements must be granted before the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 三段论中的第二个位置同样称为前提，因为两个陈述都必须先被认可，结论才成立。

senses.title: A building and its land
senses.definition: the buildings and the ground belonging to a business or an owner, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 属于某企业或业主的建筑物与土地，用复数形式
senses.example: The inspectors walked through the factory premises.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员走遍了工厂的场地。
senses.why: Legal deeds opened by describing the property set before the reader, and that list of property became the buildings themselves.
senses.whyCN: 法律契约开头先描述摆在读者面前的财产，这份财产清单后来就指建筑物本身。

senses.title: The property recited in a deed
senses.titleCN: 法律文书开头陈述的财产
senses.definition: the opening part of a legal instrument that sets out the facts and property concerned
senses.definitionCN: 法律文书开头说明相关事实与财产的部分
senses.example: The lease recites the premises before stating the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 这份租约在说明租金之前先陈述标的财产。
senses.why: The word names what is placed in front of the operative clauses, so it labels that opening recital.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指放在操作性条款之前的内容，因此用来指开头的陈述部分。

senses.title: A condition treated as given
senses.titleCN: 模型中当作给定的条件
senses.definition: a condition that a model or calculation accepts as fixed before it begins
senses.definitionCN: 模型或计算在开始之前就当作固定条件的设定
senses.example: The estimate rests on the premise that fuel prices stay flat.
senses.exampleCN: 这一估算建立在燃料价格持平的假设之上。
senses.why: A model must fix something before it can move, and whatever is fixed is literally placed in front.
senses.whyCN: 模型必须先固定某些东西才能运转，被固定者正被摆在最前面。

senses.title: A claim a debate must grant
senses.titleCN: 辩论中须先接受的主张
senses.definition: a statement that one side asks the other to accept before the exchange can proceed
senses.definitionCN: 一方要求另一方在交锋开始前先接受的主张
senses.example: The judge asked whether both sides shared that premise.
senses.exampleCN: 主持人问双方是否共有那个前提。
senses.why: Debate is an argument built in public, so it needs a floor of agreed statements under it.
senses.whyCN: 辩论是当众搭建的论证，因此需要一层公认陈述作地板。

senses.title: To state something beforehand
senses.definition: to set something out in advance as a basis for what follows
senses.definitionCN: 事先把某内容摆出来，作为后续论述的基础
senses.example: Let me premise my answer with one condition.
senses.exampleCN: 请允许我先以一个条件作为回答的前提。
senses.why: The verb kept the Latin sense of sending something ahead, and English uses it rarely, mostly in formal prose.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语「事先送出」的意思，英语中很少用，多见于正式书面语。

intro.en: Premise comes from Latin praemissa, things sent before, from praemittere, to send ahead. Logic took the word for the statements placed before a conclusion, and law took it for the property described at the start of a deed; the plural then became the buildings themselves.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 praemissa「事先送出之物」，出自动词「预先送出」。逻辑学用它指放在结论之前的陈述，法律用它指契约开头描述的财产，其复数随后就指建筑物本身。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or let go, and it stands behind words of sending, such as mission and transmit.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「送、放出」，英语中表示发送的词多出自它。

items.en: The prefix prae- added «in front», so the verb meant to send something ahead of what follows.
items.cn: 前缀加上「在前」，于是动词意为把某物先于后续内容送出去。

items.en: The neuter plural named the things set before a conclusion, and logic adopted it as a technical term.
items.cn: 中性复数指放在结论之前的内容，逻辑学把它采用为术语。

items.en: Translations of Aristotle fixed major and minor premise as the two statements above and below the conclusion.
items.cn: 对亚里士多德著作的翻译固定了「大前提」与「小前提」，即结论之上与之下的两个陈述。

items.en: Deeds opened by reciting the property, and the plural premises came to mean that property and then the buildings on it.
items.cn: 契约开头先陈述财产，复数形式便指该财产，随后又指其上的建筑物。

items.en: The building sense now lives almost entirely in the plural, while the logic sense keeps the singular; the split's exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 建筑物义如今几乎只存在于复数，逻辑义则保留单数；两者分开的确切年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the same Latin root or looks close; the second group names other starting points of reasoning.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一拉丁词根或形近；第二组指推理的其他起点。

entries.definition: The plural noun for a building and its land, from the property clause of a deed.
entries.definitionCN: 指房屋及场地，来自契约中的财产条款。

entries.definition: Based on a stated assumption; the past participle used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指以某陈述假设为基础的，是过去分词作形容词。

entries.definition: The older spelling used in logic for a stated proposition.
entries.definitionCN: 逻辑学中指前提命题的旧拼写。

entries.definition: First in rank; it belongs to the Latin word for first, not to sending ahead.
entries.definitionCN: 指地位最高的；属于拉丁语「第一」，与「预先送出」无关。

entries.definition: A bonus or an insurance payment; it comes from the word for reward.
entries.definitionCN: 指奖金或保险费；来自表示报酬的词。

entries.definition: A declaration that one will do something; its root is to send forth a word, a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指表示将做某事的声明；其词根是「送出话语」，属另一动词。

entries.definition: Something accepted as true without evidence, often silently.
entries.definitionCN: 指无证据而被接受为真的东西，常是默许的。

entries.definition: A belief that must already hold for a statement to make sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个陈述要成立就必须先已存在的信念。

entries.definition: A statement that can be judged true or false.
entries.definitionCN: 指可判断真假的陈述。

entries.definition: A tentative explanation offered for testing, not merely granted.
entries.definitionCN: 指提出来供检验的暂时解释，而不只是被认可。

entries.definition: A principle accepted without proof as a starting point.
entries.definitionCN: 指无需证明即被接受作为出发点的原理。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the table-leg picture, the syllogism slots, the legal deed and the everyday plural.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用桌腿画面、三段论的两个位置、法律契约与日常复数用法。

normal.en: A premise is sent before the conclusion, just as a table leg is placed before the table top.
normal.cn: 前提先于结论送出，正如桌腿先于桌面立好。

normal.en: The major premise is the wide statement; the minor premise puts one case under it.
normal.cn: 大前提是宽的一般陈述，小前提把一个事例放到它下面。

normal.en: Premises in the plural are buildings, from the property clause at the head of a deed.
normal.cn: 复数形式指建筑物，来自契约开头的财产条款。

normal.en: A false premise makes a valid argument reach a wrong conclusion.
normal.cn: 前提错了，形式有效的论证也会得出错误结论。

normal.en: On the premise that is the everyday phrase that carries the logic sense into ordinary writing.
normal.cn: 「以……为前提」是把逻辑义带入日常写作的固定说法。

abstract.en: A premise is a floor that nobody looks at until the argument falls through it.
abstract.cn: 前提是一块地板，直到论证掉了下去，才有人低头看它。

abstract.en: Every model stands on statements it never proves, and that silence is what makes it usable.
abstract.cn: 每个模型都站在它从不证明的陈述上，正是这份沉默让它可用。

abstract.en: The same word can name a sentence and a building, because both are things set in front of you.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能指一句话，也能指一栋楼，因为两者都是摆在你面前的东西。

examples.en: The study rests on the premise that memory declines with age.
examples.cn: 这项研究建立在记忆随年龄衰退这一前提上。

examples.en: If the premise is false, the conclusion cannot stand.
examples.cn: 如果前提错误，结论就站不住。

examples.en: Visitors must not smoke anywhere on the premises.
examples.cn: 访客不得在场地内任何地方吸烟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「普瑞密斯」——「普」通人先「密」密接受的那句话，就是推理的前提

root: 拉丁语 praemissa「事先送出之物」← praemittere「预先送出」= prae-「在前」+ mittere「送、放」。逻辑学经中世纪翻译固定「大前提、小前提」，法律契约开头的财产陈述引申出「房屋及场地」。十五世纪起见于英语；两义分化的确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from logic to property: a supporting proposition, an untested assumption, the major and minor premises, buildings and land, a deed recital, a fixed model condition, a debated claim, and the rare verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从逻辑延伸到财产：支撑命题、未验证假设、大前提、小前提、房屋场地、契约陈述、模型条件、辩论主张，以及少用的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four legs are set down first, and only then can the stacked cards of argument rest on the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：先放下四条桌腿，论证的卡片堆才放得上桌面。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT FLOOR: the proposition that must be granted before debate can proceed.
branches.cn: 论证的地板：辩论开始前必须先被认可的那个命题。

branches.en: THE UNPROVED GRANT: assumptions that a person or a model simply accepts.
branches.cn: 未经证明的认可：人或模型直接接受的假设。

branches.en: THE TWO LOGIC SLOTS: the general statement and the case placed under it.
branches.cn: 逻辑的两个位置：一般陈述与置于其下的事例。

branches.en: THE LEGAL PROPERTY: the recited property and the buildings standing on it.
branches.cn: 法律上的财产：契约陈述的财产及其上的建筑物。

branches.en: THE RARE VERB: to send a condition ahead as a basis.
branches.cn: 少用的动词义：事先把一个条件送出作为基础。

intro.en: Premise is a Latin participle turned noun, and the same root that sends things ahead also produced words of mission and transmission.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语分词转成的名词，同一个「预先送出」词根也产生了「使命」「传送」等词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies praemittere and praemissa; the logic and property senses both grew from the idea of things placed in front.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「预先送出」与「事先送出之物」；逻辑义与财产义都从「摆在前面之物」长出来。

items.example: It marks what is sent ahead.
items.exampleCN: 它标出事先送出的东西。

items.example: The root of mission and transmit.
items.exampleCN: 这是「使命」与「传送」的词根。

items.example: The direct source of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这是该名词的直接来源。

items.example: It became the logic term for a premise.
It marks the rare English verb premise.
items.exampleCN: 它标明这个少用的英语动词。

items.example: The legal sense moved into everyday property talk.
items.exampleCN: 法律义进入日常财产用语。

items.meaning: a statement set before a conclusion
items.example: The everyday singular that carries the logic sense.
items.exampleCN: 这是承载逻辑义的日常单数形式。

items.example: It survives chiefly in British academic prose.
items.exampleCN: 它主要保留在英国学术写作中。

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「房屋及场地」
加已然词尾，义为「以……为基础的」
逻辑学旧拼写，义为「前提」
复合形容词，义为「以前提为基础的」

definition_zh: 准备；预备；配制品；（复数）筹备工作
definition_en: the act of making something or someone ready, or a substance made ready for a particular use
core_image: 厨房案板上一排切好的食材、一张写满步骤的纸，锅还没上火
scene: 这场考试的准备工作比考试本身花的时间还长。Preparation for the exam took longer than the exam itself.
sceneCN: 这里 preparation 是「准备工作、预备」（第 1 个义项：使事情就绪的过程）；句意：备考所花的时间比考试本身还长。图中可辨识物件：切好的食材、步骤纸、尚未点火的锅；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 准备；预备；配制品；筹备工作

derivatives.zh: 准备；预备
准备好的
预备的
有助于准备的
没有准备的
（口语）准备；预习

senses.title: Making ready
senses.titleCN: 准备：把事情弄成就绪状态
senses.definition: the process of getting something or someone ready for what is to come
senses.definitionCN: 使某物或某人就绪以应对将来之事的过程
senses.example: Preparation of the venue began three days early.
senses.exampleCN: 场地准备工作提前三天开始。
senses.why: prae- 'before' plus parare 'make ready' gives praeparare, 'to make ready beforehand'. The noun names that before-work.
senses.whyCN: prae-“在前”加 parare“使就绪”构成 praeparare“预先使就绪”，名词命名这件“提前做的事”。

senses.title: The state of readiness
senses.definition: the condition of being ready, considered as a result rather than an activity
senses.definitionCN: 已经就绪的状态，被视为结果而非活动
senses.example: The troops were in preparation for a night march.
senses.exampleCN: 部队正处于夜行军的准备状态。
senses.why: The same -ation noun can name the result as well as the process, so preparation can be a state one is in.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 -ation 名词既可命名过程也可命名结果，所以 preparation 也可以是一种所处的状态。

senses.title: Study beforehand
senses.definition: work done in advance to learn or to be able to teach a subject
senses.definitionCN: 为学会或能够讲授某科目而提前做的工夫
senses.example: Her lesson preparation takes two hours a night.
senses.exampleCN: 她每晚备课要花两个小时。
senses.why: Teaching turns preparation into a private, daily task: the teacher must be ready before the class exists.
senses.whyCN: 教学把准备变成私人的日常功课：课还不存在时，老师就得先就绪。

senses.title: A medicinal preparation
senses.definition: a substance, especially a medicine or cosmetic, compounded into a usable form
senses.definitionCN: 调配成可用形态的物质，尤指药物或化妆品
senses.example: The pharmacy makes a preparation for dry skin.
senses.exampleCN: 这家药房配制一种用于干性皮肤的制剂。
senses.why: Pharmacists prepare mixtures, so the product of that work took the name of the work. A preparation is readiness made tangible.
senses.whyCN: 药剂师调配混合物，于是产物沿用了动作的名字。制剂就是被做成实物的“就绪”。

senses.title: Laboratory preparation
senses.titleCN: 实验室制备：把样本弄成能看的样子
senses.definition: the treatment of a specimen or chemical so that it can be examined or used
senses.definitionCN: 对标本或化学品进行处理，使其可被观察或使用
senses.example: Slide preparation must be done within an hour of sampling.
senses.exampleCN: 玻片制备必须在采样后一小时内完成。
senses.why: In the lab the word names a technical routine: tissue, soil or a compound is made ready for the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里，这个词命名一套技术流程：组织、土壤或化合物被做成适合仪器的样子。

senses.title: Food preparation
senses.titleCN: 食品加工：把原料做成饭
senses.definition: the cleaning, cutting and cooking of food before it is eaten
senses.definitionCN: 食物食用前的清洗、切配与烹制
senses.example: Food preparation areas must be kept separate from toilets.
senses.exampleCN: 食品加工区必须与卫生间分开。
senses.why: Cooking is preparation in the oldest sense: raw material is made ready to be consumed.
senses.whyCN: 烹饪是最古老意义上的准备：原料被做成可以入口的样子。

senses.title: Music: preparing a dissonance
senses.titleCN: 音乐：为不协和音做铺垫
senses.definition: in counterpoint, the earlier sounding of a note that will later form a dissonance
senses.definitionCN: 对位法中，某音先以协和状态出现，随后才构成不协和
senses.example: The suspension needs a preparation in the preceding chord.
senses.exampleCN: 延留音需要在前面和弦中有铺垫。
senses.why: Music theory borrowed the everyday word literally: the ear is prepared for the clash by hearing the note first in peace.
senses.whyCN: 乐理字面借用了日常词：先让耳朵在协和中听到该音，为后面的冲突做准备。

senses.title: Arrangements, plural
senses.definition: the practical arrangements made in advance, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 提前做出的一项项实际安排，通常用复数
senses.example: The wedding preparations filled the whole summer.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼筹备占满了整个夏天。
senses.why: Countable plural preparations names the individual items of the before-work: bookings, lists, orders.
senses.whyCN: 可数复数 preparations 命名提前工作中的一件件具体事项：预订、清单、订单。

intro.en: Preparation comes from Latin praeparare 'to make ready beforehand', from prae- 'before' plus parare 'make ready, furnish'. The noun is praeparatio.
intro.cn: preparation 来自拉丁 praeparare“预先使就绪”，由 prae-“在前”加 parare“使就绪、置办”构成，名词为 praeparatio。

items.en: parare meant 'to make ready, prepare, furnish'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; it is generally connected with a PIE root *pere- 'to produce, procure', which should be labelled as generally believed rather than certain.
items.cn: parare 意为“使就绪、预备、置办”。其更深来源不确定，一般认为与原始印欧语词根 *pere-“产出、取得”有关，应标“一般认为是”而非确定。

items.en: prae- 'before' plus parare produced praeparare, 'to get ready in advance'. The prefix adds time, not place.
items.cn: prae-“在前”加 parare 构成 praeparare“提前弄好”。前缀加的是时间，不是地点。

items.en: The action noun praeparatio named both the act of readying and the state of being ready.
items.cn: 动作名词 praeparatio 既指“使就绪的行为”，也指“已就绪的状态”。

items.en: English borrows preparation in the 1300s through French, first in religious writing about preparing the soul.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪经法语借入 preparation，最早见于关于心灵预备的宗教写作。

items.en: From the 16th century a preparation is also a compound made ready by an apothecary, which is why the word can name a medicine.
items.cn: 16 世纪起，preparation 也指药剂师配好的复方，因此这个词可以命名一种药。

items.en: In modern English the word covers exam study, food handling, lab routines and event arrangements, all sharing the same before-work.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词覆盖备考、食品处理、实验室流程与活动筹备，共享同一件“提前做的事”。

note.en: The look-alike group shares par- or the pre- prefix; the near-meaning group also involves getting ready but differs in what is being readied.
note.cn: 形近组共享 par- 或 pre- 前缀；近义组也涉及就绪，差别在“让什么就绪”。

entries.definition: to make ready. The verb is the act; the noun is the act or its product.
entries.definitionCN: 准备。动词是动作，名词是动作或其产物。

entries.definition: introducing or leading up to something main. It describes position in a sequence, not the work itself.
entries.definitionCN: 预备的；作为前导的。它描述顺序中的位置，而非准备工作本身。

entries.definition: a public procession. It comes from French parade 'display', from parer 'to adorn, arrange', a different branch of parare's sense range.
entries.definitionCN: 游行；阅兵。来自法语 parade“展示”，源于 parer“装饰、布置”，是 parare 词义范围中的另一分支。

entries.definition: the state of being prepared. It names only the condition, while preparation can also name the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 就绪状态。它只命名状态，而 preparation 还能命名活动。

entries.definition: the way things are put in order, or the plans made. It stresses organisation rather than readiness.
entries.definitionCN: 安排；布置。强调组织，而非就绪。

entries.definition: long instruction to build skill. It is preparation for a role, but it names the skill-building, not the readying.
entries.definitionCN: 训练。它是为某角色做的准备，但命名的是技能培养，而非就绪。

entries.definition: the basic work that makes later work possible. It is a kind of preparation, but stresses foundation.
entries.definitionCN: 基础工作。它是准备的一种，但强调打地基。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: pre- 'before' plus parare 'make ready' gives the whole idea: ready made before it is needed.
normal.cn: pre-“在前”加 parare“使就绪”，整个意思就出来了：在需要之前先弄好。

normal.en: The family prepare, prepared, preparatory, preparation all keep the par- stem.
normal.cn: prepare、prepared、preparatory、preparation 全族保留 par- 词干。

normal.en: A medicinal preparation is the pharmacist's work turned into a bottle.
normal.cn: 药物制剂就是药剂师的工作变成一瓶东西。

normal.en: In preparation for is the most common frame and always points forward in time.
normal.cn: “为……做准备”是最常见的框架，永远指向未来的时间。

normal.en: The opposite state is unprepared, which is simply readiness missing.
normal.cn: 反面的状态是 unprepared，就是“就绪”缺席。

abstract.en: Picture a stage set the night before, lit but empty.
abstract.cn: 想象演出前一晚的舞台：灯亮着，台上没人。

abstract.en: Picture a bag packed by the door, waiting for the morning.
abstract.cn: 想象门口放着一个收好的包，等天亮。

abstract.en: Picture a chess player arranging pieces before the clock starts.
abstract.cn: 想象棋手在计时开始前摆好棋子。

examples.en: Careful preparation saved the expedition from the storm.
examples.cn: 周密的准备使探险队免于风暴之灾。

examples.en: The lab keeps a preparation of the enzyme at four degrees.
examples.cn: 实验室在四摄氏度下保存该酶的制剂。

examples.en: Most of the work was preparation, not performance.
examples.cn: 大部分工作是准备，而不是表演。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞帕瑞”音近 preparation：普普通通也要先摆好、排一排——提前把东西弄齐 → preparation 准备

root: 拉丁 prae-“在前”+ parare“使就绪、置办”（parare 更深来源不确定，一般认为出自印欧 *pere-“产出”）；praeparatio(n-) 词干 + -ion。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe work done before the main event, sometimes the work and sometimes what the work produced.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述“主事之前做的功”，有时指功夫本身，有时指功夫的产物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a workbench laid out before anything is cooked.
core.cn: 核心意象：还没开火就已摆好的案板。

branches.en: ACT AND STATE: preparation names the process and the readiness it produces.
branches.cn: 行为与状态：preparation 命名过程以及它带来的就绪。

branches.en: DAILY READYING: lesson preparation and food preparation are both private, repeated before-work.
branches.cn: 日常就绪：备课与备餐都是私人的、反复的提前功夫。

branches.en: MADE SUBSTANCE: a medicine and a microscope slide are the noun's product side.
branches.cn: 制成之物：药剂与玻片是这个词的产物面。

branches.en: MUSIC: counterpoint prepares the ear for a clash by sounding the note first in peace.
branches.cn: 音乐：对位法先让音在协和中出现，为耳朵预备冲突。

branches.en: PLANS: countable preparations are the individual arrangements of the before-work.
branches.cn: 计划：可数复数指提前工作中的一件件安排。

intro.en: Preparation is prae- plus parare plus -ion. The prefix marks 'before', the verb marks 'readying', and the suffix turns it into a noun of action or result.
intro.cn: preparation 由 prae- 加 parare 加 -ion 构成。前缀标记“在前”，动词标记“使就绪”，后缀使其成为动作或结果名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin line is parare 'make ready' → praeparare 'prepare' → praeparatio 'a preparing'. English also keeps the adjective stem in preparatory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁线为 parare“使就绪”→ praeparare“准备”→ praeparatio“预备”。英语还在 preparatory 中保留形容词词干。

items.example: She prepared the room for the guests.
items.exampleCN: 她为客人准备好了房间。

items.meaning: the act or result of readying

items.exampleCN: 他就读于一所预备学校。

items.example: We were prepared for the worst.
items.exampleCN: 我们做好了最坏的准备。

items.meaningCN: 有助于准备的（-ive 表性质，现罕用）

items.meaning: informal for preparation or preparatory school
items.example: He did his prep before dinner.
items.exampleCN: 他在晚饭前做完了预习。

items.meaning: the state of being ready, especially for emergencies
items.meaningCN: 戒备状态；应急准备（-ness 状态名词）
items.exampleCN: 该机构推动灾害应急准备。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 使就绪；置办；取得（更深来源不确定）

definition_zh: 准备；预备；使做好准备；配制；编写；筹备
definition_en: to make someone or something ready for what will happen, to put a dish or mixture together, or to draw up a plan or text
core_image: 案板上一排切好的菜，锅已烧热，手正把盐罐拉到近前
scene: 天还没亮，厨房的灯先亮了，她把米淘好放进锅里。She prepared a simple breakfast before the children woke.
sceneCN: 这里 prepare 是「配制、做好（饭菜）」（第 2 个义项：把食材做成可以吃的东西）；句意为她在孩子们醒来之前做好了一顿简单的早饭。图中可辨识物件：案板、切好的菜、热锅、盐罐。

pos.zh: 准备；预备；使做好准备；配制；编写

derivatives.zh: 由 prepare 换用名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「准备；准备工作」
由拉丁词干 preparat- 加 -ory 构成，义为「预备的；筹备的」
由 prepare 加 -ed 构成，义为「有准备的；事先做好的」
由 prepared 加 -ness 构成，义为「有准备的状态；戒备」

senses.title: To get ready before something happens
senses.definition: to make yourself or something else ready for an event that is still to come
senses.definitionCN: 让自己或别的事物为尚未到来的事情进入就绪状态
senses.example: The team spent the morning preparing for the match.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍花了一上午为比赛做准备。
senses.why: Latin parare meant to make ready, and prae- adds the idea of doing it beforehand, so preparation is readiness produced in advance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 parare 意为使就绪，prae- 又加上「事先」的意思，所以 preparation 就是提前造出来的就绪状态。

senses.title: To put a dish or mixture together
senses.definition: to combine ingredients and make them ready to eat or to use
senses.definitionCN: 把各种材料组合起来，做成可以吃或可以用的东西
senses.example: He prepared a pot of soup for the guests.
senses.exampleCN: 他为客人煮了一锅汤。
senses.why: Making a dish ready is the same act of putting things in order, so the verb moves from readiness in general to the kitchen without changing its core.
senses.whyCN: 把一道菜弄好，仍然是同样的「把东西整理到位」的动作，所以这个词从一般的就绪转到厨房，核心并没有变。

senses.title: To train or equip someone for a task
senses.definition: to give a person the knowledge or experience needed for a future task
senses.definitionCN: 让某人为将来的任务获得所需的知识或经验
senses.example: The course prepares students for work in a real lab.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课让学生为在真实实验室里工作做好准备。
senses.why: When the object is a person, readiness becomes training, and the verb names what teaching does before the test of real work.
senses.whyCN: 当宾语是人时，就绪就变成了训练，这个词命名的正是教学在真实工作检验之前所做的那一步。

senses.title: To draw up a text or plan
senses.definition: to write or compose a document, plan or set of figures in advance
senses.definitionCN: 提前写出或编写成文件、方案或一组数字
senses.example: She prepared a short report for the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她为会议写了一份简短报告。
senses.why: A document is also made ready before it is used, which is why the verb covers drawing up papers as well as cooking.
senses.whyCN: 文件在使用之前同样要先被弄好，所以这个词既能指做饭，也能指起草文书。

intro.en: Prepare is a Latin verb of making ready with a prefix meaning beforehand, filtered through Old French, and English widened it to meals, lessons, reports and medicine.
intro.cn: prepare 是一个加上「事先」前缀的拉丁「使就绪」动词，经古法语传入，英语又把它扩展到饭菜、功课、报告与药物。

items.en: Parare meant to make ready, to furnish or to put something in order; its deeper origin is uncertain and is usually left open.
items.cn: parare 意为使就绪、置办或把东西整理好；它更早的来源不确定，一般认为难以定论。

items.en: Prae- means before, so praeparare meant to get something ready ahead of the moment it would be needed.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在……之前」，praeparare 便指在需要之前就把事情弄好。

items.en: The participle praeparatus, made ready, supplied adjective and noun forms that later languages reused.
items.cn: 分词 praeparatus 意为「已备好的」，后来的语言沿用了它提供的形容词与名词形式。

items.en: Old French kept the verb as preparer, and English borrowed it in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词保留为 preparer，英语在中世纪将其借入。

items.en: Modern English widened prepare to meals, lessons, reports and medicine, all sharing the idea of readiness made in advance.
items.cn: 现代英语把 prepare 扩展到饭菜、功课、报告与药物，这些用法共享「提前备好」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same Latin verb of readiness; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for getting things and people into position.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「使就绪」动词的形式；近义组收表示把事物与人安排到位的动词。

entries.definition: The act or process of getting ready, or a substance made ready for use.
entries.definitionCN: 由 prepare 转成的名词，指准备的过程，或配好的制剂。

entries.definition: Serving to get something ready, as in a preparatory course.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的形容词，义为预备的，如预科课程。

entries.definition: Ready, or made in advance rather than at the moment.
entries.definitionCN: 由 prepare 加 -ed 构成，义为有准备的、事先做好的。

entries.definition: To mend something; it comes from re- plus parare, to make ready again, so the root is shared but the meaning has moved.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的另一支，由 re- 加 parare（重新弄好）构成，词根相同但词义已转向修理。

entries.definition: To make something or someone completely prepared, used mostly in technical and military writing.
entries.definitionCN: 使完全就绪；多用于技术与军事文字。

entries.definition: To put things in a particular order or make plans for them.
entries.definitionCN: 安排；把事物按某种次序放好或作出计划。

entries.definition: To plan and put the parts of an activity into working order.
entries.definitionCN: 组织；把一项活动的各部分计划并安排妥当。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin verb of readiness with a prefix of time, and its family keeps returning to what is done before the moment of use.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是带时间前缀的拉丁「使就绪」动词，同族词反复回到「在使用之前先做好」这件事。

normal.en: Parare means to make ready, and prae- adds before, so prepare is literally to ready something beforehand.
normal.cn: parare 意为使就绪，prae- 加上「之前」，所以 prepare 字面上就是提前把某事弄好。

normal.en: Preparation is the noun from the same stem, naming the whole process rather than the single act.
normal.cn: preparation 是同一词干的名词，指整个过程，而不只是单个动作。

normal.en: Prepared can be an adjective, which is why we say someone is well prepared.
normal.cn: prepared 也可以作形容词，所以可以说某人有充分准备。

normal.en: Repair shares the same parare but with re-, to make ready again, and has drifted to mending.
normal.cn: repair 同样用 parare，但带 re-（重新弄好），词义已漂移到修理。

normal.en: Prepare a meal and prepare a report both mean putting parts in order before they are needed.
normal.cn: prepare a meal 与 prepare a report 都指在需要之前把各部分整理到位。

abstract.en: To prepare is to work in the present on behalf of a moment that has not arrived.
abstract.cn: 准备就是在当下为尚未到来的时刻做事。

abstract.en: The word assumes the future will ask something of you, and it answers before the question is spoken.
abstract.cn: 这个词假定未来会向你提出要求，并在问题说出口之前就先作答。

abstract.en: Cooking, teaching and writing all appear under one verb because all three are ways of arranging the world in advance.
abstract.cn: 做饭、教学与写作都归到同一个动词下，因为三者都是提前把世界安排好的方式。

examples.en: She prepared a simple breakfast before the children woke.
examples.cn: 她在孩子们醒来之前做好了一顿简单的早饭。

examples.en: The team spent the morning preparing for the match.
examples.cn: 队伍花了一上午为比赛做准备。

examples.en: The course prepares students for work in a real lab.
examples.cn: 这门课让学生为在真实实验室里工作做好准备。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑瑞派」——先把人派到前面去等着；prepare 就是准备、预备。

root: 源自拉丁语 parare（使就绪、置办），加前缀 prae-（在前、事先）构成 praeparare，经分词 praeparatus 与古法语 preparer 进入英语；同族词有 preparation、preparatory，repair 亦出同一 parare。

sensesIntro.en: The core is readiness made in advance; the senses divide into general preparation, cooking, training people, and drawing up papers.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是提前造出的就绪状态；义项由此分出一般准备、做饭配药、训练人员，以及起草文书。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of chopped vegetables on a board, the pan already hot, a hand reaching for the salt.
core.cn: 核心意象：案板上一排切好的菜，锅已烧热，手正把盐罐拉到近前。

branches.en: a bag packed the night before a journey
branches.cn: 出发前一夜就收拾好的包

branches.en: vegetables cut and waiting beside a hot pan
branches.cn: 切好放在热锅旁的蔬菜

branches.en: a student practising on a lab bench before the test
branches.cn: 考试前在实验台上练习的学生

branches.en: a report laid on the table before the meeting starts
branches.cn: 会议开始前摆在桌上的报告

branches.en: a cook reading the recipe once before starting
branches.cn: 开火前先把菜谱看一遍的厨师

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of readiness plus a prefix of time, and English added suffixes that turn it into a process, an adjective and a state.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示「使就绪」的拉丁动词加上时间前缀，英语又添上后缀，使它变成过程、形容词与状态。

latinIntro.en: Prepare goes back to Latin praeparare, from prae- and parare, to make ready; the participle praeparatus and the noun praeparatio carry the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: prepare 上溯拉丁语 praeparare，由 prae- 与 parare（使就绪）构成；分词 praeparatus 与名词 praeparatio 用的是同一词干。

definition_zh: 出席；在场；存在；风度；气场
definition_en: the state of being in a place or of existing, and the impression a person makes by being there
core_image: 空椅子旁忽然多了一个人，屋里的人不自觉地把目光移过去
scene: 会议室里人到齐了，主位还空着，门一响，那位迟到的顾问走进来，屋里立刻安静。Her presence at the meeting made everyone sit up straight.
sceneCN: 这里 presence 指「在场、出席」（第 1 个义项：人就在现场）；句意为她一出现在会上，所有人就坐直了。图中可辨识场景：长桌、空着的主位、刚进门的顾问。

derivatives.zh: 与 presence 同出拉丁语 praesens，义为「在场的；现在的」
由 present 加 -ly 构成，义为「不久；目前」
由 omni-（全部）与 presence 复合，义为「无所不在」

senses.title: The state of being in a particular place
senses.definition: the fact of being in a place and not absent
senses.definitionCN: 身处某地、没有缺席的事实
senses.example: Your presence at the ceremony would mean a lot to her.
senses.exampleCN: 你若出席典礼，对她意义重大。
senses.why: The Latin participle praesens means being before someone's eyes, so the first sense is simply the body being there.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语分词 praesens 意为「在某人眼前」，所以最基本的义项就是身体确实在那里，能被看见。

senses.title: The fact that something exists in a place
senses.definition: the fact that a substance, quality, or thing exists in a particular place or situation
senses.definitionCN: 某种物质、性质或事物存在于某处或某种情况之中
senses.example: Tests confirmed the presence of mercury in the water.
senses.exampleCN: 检测确认水中存在汞。
senses.why: If being before the eyes is the core, then anything that makes itself detectable is said to be present, even when it cannot be seen.
senses.whyCN: 既然核心是「出现在眼前」，那么任何能被察觉的东西都可以说成 present，即使肉眼看不见，细菌、汞也能「在场」。

senses.title: The impression made by a person's manner
senses.definition: the quality of a person's manner and bearing that makes others notice or respect them
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的举止与仪态给人留下印象、令人注意或敬重的气质
senses.example: The young actor has remarkable stage presence.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻演员有出众的舞台魅力。
senses.why: A person who fills a room simply by standing there seems to turn visible being into influence, which is why the word comes to mean bearing.
senses.whyCN: 一个人只站着就撑满整个房间，等于把「被看见的存在」变成一种影响力，于是这个词从「在场」长出了「气场」。

senses.title: A person or thing that is present but not seen
senses.definition: a person or thing that is in a place, especially one felt rather than seen, such as a spirit or a military force
senses.definitionCN: 身处某处的人或物，尤指只能感觉到而看不见的，如幽灵或军事力量
senses.example: She felt a strange presence in the empty house.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得空房子里有个奇怪的存在。
senses.why: Once the word can name any detectable thing, an unseen figure or a foreign army also counts as a presence, because what matters is the effect, not the visibility.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能指任何可察觉之物，看不见的身影或驻扎的外国军队也能叫 presence，因为重点是它造成的影响，而不是能否看见。

intro.en: Presence comes from a Latin prefix meaning before joined to the verb to be; it names, quite literally, the state of being before someone.
intro.cn: presence 来自表示「在前」的拉丁前缀与动词「存在」的组合，字面上就是「在某人面前存在」的状态。

items.en: Prae- meant before or in front, the same prefix that marks what stands ahead of us.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在前面」，用来标示站在我们之前的东西。

items.en: Esse was the verb to be, the source of many forms in the Latin verb system and one of its oldest words.
items.cn: esse 是表示「存在、是」的动词，也是拉丁语动词系统中最古老的一组形式之一。

items.en: Praesens, the participle of praeesse, described what is before one, at hand, or in sight.
items.cn: praesens 是 praeesse 的分词，描述「在某人面前、在手边、在视野中」的东西。

items.en: The noun praesentia named the state of being there, and it passed into Old French as presence.
items.cn: 名词 praesentia 指「在场」的状态，进入古法语后写作 presence。

items.en: English uses presence for a body in a room, for anything that exists, and for the impression a person carries.
items.cn: 现代英语用 presence 指人在屋里、事物存在，以及一个人带来的气场。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin participle of being; the near-meaning group gathers words for attendance, existence and personal bearing.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「存在」的拉丁分词；近义组收出席、存在与个人气质方面的词。

entries.definition: Being in a place, or existing now.
entries.definitionCN: 在场的；现在的。

entries.definition: Soon, or at the present time.
entries.definitionCN: 不久；目前。

entries.definition: The state of being everywhere at once.
entries.definitionCN: 无所不在的状态。

entries.definition: Knowledge of events before they happen; the word comes from another root meaning to know, so it is only similar in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 预知未来的能力；此词来自另一表示「知道」的词根，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The act of being present at an event.
entries.definitionCN: 出席活动的行为。

entries.definition: The state of being real or alive.
entries.definitionCN: 真实存在或生存的状态。

entries.definition: A quality that seems to surround a person.
entries.definitionCN: 似乎环绕在人身周的气质。

entries.definition: The way a person stands and moves.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的站姿与举止。

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin verb to be with a prefix meaning before, and its family keeps measuring how close something is to the room.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是表示「存在」的拉丁动词加表示「在前」的前缀，同族词都在衡量某物离这个房间有多近。

normal.en: Pre- plus esse: presence is literally being before someone, which is why the word starts with the body in the room.
normal.cn: pre- 加 esse：presence 字面就是「在某人面前存在」，所以起点是身体在屋里。

normal.en: Absent is the same verb with ab-, away: away from being, therefore not in the room.
normal.cn: absent 是同一个动词加 ab-（离开）：离开存在，因此不在屋里。

normal.en: The adjective present and the noun presence share one Latin participle, which is why both point to being here.
normal.cn: 形容词 present 与名词 presence 共用一个拉丁分词，所以都指向「在这里」。

normal.en: Presently can mean soon because what is at hand is about to arrive.
normal.cn: presently 能表示「不久」，因为在手边的东西马上就要到了。

normal.en: Omnipresence joins omni-, all, to presence: being everywhere at once.
normal.cn: omnipresence 把表示「全部」的 omni- 与 presence 结合，就是同时无所不在。

abstract.en: A room feels different the moment one person walks in, and that change is exactly what the word names.
abstract.cn: 一个人走进来的瞬间，屋里的感觉就变了，这个词命名的正是这种变化。

abstract.en: Presence is being seen without speaking: no words, only the fact of occupying space.
abstract.cn: presence 是不说话也被看见：没有言语，只有占据空间这件事。

abstract.en: The same root gives absent and present, so the word measures distance from the room.
abstract.cn: 同一个词根给出 absent 与 present，这个词量的其实是离房间的距离。

examples.en: Her presence at the meeting made everyone sit up straight.
examples.cn: 她一出现在会上，所有人就坐直了。

examples.en: The doctor noted the presence of a slight fever.
examples.cn: 医生注意到有轻微发热。

examples.en: The old house seemed to hold a presence of its own.
examples.cn: 这座老房子似乎自有一种存在感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音近「普瑞森斯」——贵人一到场，森森的安静就跟着来，presence 就是那种在场感。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ esse（存在）→ praesens（在眼前的）→ praesentia（在场），经古法语 presence 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being before someone's eyes; the senses run from a body in the room to anything that exists, then to the impression a person leaves.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「出现在某人眼前」；义项从人在屋里，扩展到任何事物的存在，再到一个人留下的气场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one more figure standing in a room that was already full.
core.cn: 核心意象：原本坐满的房间里，多出一个站着的人。

branches.en: a chair pulled out for the late guest
branches.cn: 为迟到的客人拉开一把椅子

branches.en: a test strip changing colour in a glass of water
branches.cn: 试纸在一杯水里变色

branches.en: a silent actor who owns the stage without a line
branches.cn: 不发一言却撑住舞台的演员

branches.en: a cold spot in a house nobody wants to enter
branches.cn: 无人敢进的屋子里那块冷处

branches.en: a quiet arrival that changes the mood of the room
branches.cn: 一次安静的到场改变了屋里的气氛

intro.en: The word rests on the Latin verb to be, its participle, and two English endings that turn the state into a noun and related adjectives.
intro.cn: 这个词依托拉丁语动词「存在」、它的分词，以及把状态变成名词和相关形容词的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: not here, formed with ab- away

definition_zh: 现在的；目前的；出席的；在场的；礼物；提出；呈现
definition_en: existing or happening now; being in a place; a gift; and to give, show, or put something before others
core_image: 一只手把东西伸到另一个人面前：此刻、此地、就在眼前
scene: 年会上，主持人把一个包装好的盒子递到老员工手里，全场鼓掌。The retiring engineer received a small present from the whole team.
sceneCN: 这里 present 是名词「礼物」（第 3 个义项：送给别人的东西）；句意为即将退休的工程师收到了全队送的一件小礼物。图中可辨识物件：包装盒、彩带、鼓掌的同事。

pos.zh: 现在的；目前的；出席的；在场的

derivatives.zh: 由 present 加 -ation 构成，义为「演示；陈述；颁发」
由 present 加 -ly 构成，义为「不久；目前」
由 present 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「主持人；演示者」
由 present 加 -able 构成，义为「拿得出手的；像样的」

senses.title: Existing or happening now
senses.definition: existing, happening, or being considered at this moment
senses.definitionCN: 此刻存在、发生或正在被考虑的
senses.example: The present situation calls for patience.
senses.exampleCN: 目前的形势需要耐心。
senses.why: Latin praesens describes what stands before the eyes, and what stands before the eyes is by definition what is here now.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praesens 指「摆在眼前的」，而摆在眼前的东西按定义就是此刻的，所以这个词自然有了「现在的」义。

senses.title: Being in a place rather than absent
senses.definition: being in a particular place at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 在某一时间身处某一地点
senses.example: All the members were present at the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 所有成员都出席了投票。
senses.why: The same participle can describe a person as well as a moment: whoever is before us is present in the room.
senses.whyCN: 同一个分词既能修饰时刻，也能修饰人：谁在我们眼前，谁就是「在场的」。

senses.title: A thing given to someone as a gift
senses.definition: something that you give to someone, especially on a special occasion
senses.definitionCN: 赠予某人的东西，尤指在特殊场合
senses.example: She wrapped the present in blue paper.
senses.exampleCN: 她用蓝纸把礼物包了起来。
senses.why: The noun came from the idea of something placed before a person, and a gift is exactly an object set in front of someone to be taken.
senses.whyCN: 名词来自「摆到某人面前的东西」这一想法，而礼物正是被放到对方面前、请对方收下的物件，义项由此固定下来。

senses.title: To offer or submit something formally
senses.definition: to give a plan, report, or proposal to someone in authority for them to consider
senses.definitionCN: 把计划、报告或建议正式交给有权者考虑
senses.example: She presented her proposal to the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 她向委员会提出了自己的方案。
senses.why: The Latin verb praesentare meant to place before someone; putting a document before a committee is the modern version of that gesture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 praesentare 意为「放到某人面前」，把文件摆到委员会面前，就是这一动作在现代的版本。

senses.title: To show, display, or perform something
senses.definition: to show something to an audience, or to appear in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 向观众展示某物，或以某种样子出现
senses.example: The theatre will present three new plays this spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家剧院今年春天将上演三部新剧。
senses.why: Once you can place an object before people, you can also place a performance or an image before them, which is how the word reaches stages and screens.
senses.whyCN: 既然能把物件摆到人前，也就能把演出或形象摆到人前，于是这个词走上了舞台与屏幕。

intro.en: Present and presence come from the same Latin participle, but English moved the stress and stretched the meaning from being here to handing something over.
intro.cn: present 与 presence 出自同一个拉丁分词，但英语改变了重音位置，并把词义从「在这里」扩展到「把东西递过去」。

items.en: Prae- meant before or in front, and it marks whatever is put ahead of a person.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在前面」，标示被放到某人面前的东西。

items.en: Esse was the verb to be, and its participle praesens described what is present or at hand.
items.cn: esse 是表示「存在」的动词，它的分词 praesens 描述「在场的、在手边的」东西。

items.en: The verb praesentare meant to place something before someone, and so to offer or show it.
items.cn: 动词 praesentare 意为把某物放到某人面前，因此引申为呈上、展示。

items.en: Old French kept both the adjective of being here and the verb of placing something before another person.
items.cn: 古法语同时保留了「在场的」形容词与「把东西放到别人面前」的动词。

items.en: English puts the stress on the first syllable for the adjective and noun, on the second for the verb, and the meanings spread from time and place to gifts and performances.
items.cn: 现代英语让形容词与名词重音落在第一音节、动词落在第二音节，词义则从时间与地点扩展到礼物与演出。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin participle of being before; the near-meaning group gathers words for gifts, current time, and being somewhere.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「在眼前」的拉丁分词；近义组收礼物、当前时间与到场相关的词。

entries.definition: The state of being in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 在场的状态；出席。

entries.definition: A talk or display given to an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 向观众做的演示或展示。

entries.definition: Soon, or at this time.
entries.definitionCN: 不久；此刻。

entries.definition: To stand for something or speak for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 代表某物或替某人说话。

entries.definition: Something given to someone without payment.
entries.definitionCN: 无偿赠予他人的东西。

entries.definition: Happening or existing now.
entries.definitionCN: 现在发生或存在的。

entries.definition: To be at an event.
entries.definitionCN: 到场参加活动。

entries.definition: To give or propose something.
entries.definitionCN: 给予或提出某物。

normalIntro.en: One Latin participle gives both the thing that is here and the act of putting something in front of someone, and English separates them by stress.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁分词同时给出「在这里的东西」与「把东西放到别人面前的动作」，英语用重音把两者分开。

normal.en: The adjective and noun stress the first syllable, the verb the second: PREZ-unt for a thing, pri-ZENT for an action.
normal.cn: 形容词与名词重音在第一音节，动词在第二音节：指物时读前重，指动作时读后重。

normal.en: Present and presence share the Latin participle praesens, so both begin with the idea of being before someone.
normal.cn: present 与 presence 共用一个拉丁分词，起点都是「在某人面前」。

normal.en: Present as a gift is the object placed before a person, the same gesture as presenting a report.
normal.cn: 作「礼物」的 present 是被放到人前的物件，与呈交报告是同一个动作。

normal.en: At present is a fixed phrase for this moment, built on the time sense of the adjective.
normal.cn: at present 是表示「此刻」的固定说法，建立在形容词的时间义上。

normal.en: Presentation and presenter add endings to the verb, naming the act and the person who performs it.
normal.cn: presentation 与 presenter 给动词加后缀，分别命名行为与执行的人。

abstract.en: One word holds a moment, a place, a gift and a stage, because all of them are put in front of someone.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时装下时刻、地点、礼物与舞台，因为它们都被摆到了某人面前。

abstract.en: The stress moves like the meaning: first syllable for what is here, second for what you do with it.
abstract.cn: 重音随词义移动：前重指「在这里的东西」，后重指「你拿它做什么」。

abstract.en: A present is only a present once it is handed over, which is why the noun and the verb share a shape.
abstract.cn: 礼物只有递出去才成为礼物，所以名词与动词共用一个形状。

examples.en: The present situation calls for patience.
examples.cn: 目前的形势需要耐心。

examples.en: She presented her proposal to the committee.
examples.cn: 她向委员会提出了自己的方案。

examples.en: He gave her a small present before leaving.
examples.cn: 他临走前送了她一件小礼物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读起来像「pre（先）+ sent（送）」：先送到人前的是礼物，先摆到人前的是方案，present 就是「呈到面前」。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ esse（存在）→ praesens（在眼前的），经古法语 present 进入英语；形容词与名词重音在第一音节，动词重音在第二音节。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something placed before someone: time and place first, then the gift put in front of a person, then the act of laying a plan or a show before others.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「摆到某人面前」：先是时间与地点上的「在眼前」，再是递到面前的礼物，最后是把方案或演出摆到别人面前。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand holding something out toward another person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把东西伸到另一个人面前。

branches.en: a clock showing this very minute
branches.cn: 钟面停在此刻这一分钟

branches.en: a full row of chairs with nobody missing
branches.cn: 一排椅子坐满，无人缺席

branches.en: a wrapped box held out with both hands
branches.cn: 双手递出的包装盒

branches.en: a folder laid on the committee table
branches.cn: 放在委员桌上的文件夹

branches.en: a curtain rising on a new play
branches.cn: 新戏开演时升起的幕布

intro.en: The word is a Latin participle of being, its verb of placing before, and the English endings that name the act, the person and the quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「存在」的拉丁分词、表示「放到面前」的动词，以及命名行为、人物与性质的英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: the act of showing or giving

definition_zh: 演示；报告；赠予；颁发；呈现方式；首演
definition_en: a talk in which someone shows and explains something to an audience; also the act of giving something formally, the way something appears, or a first public performance
core_image: 讲台前的人把图表转向观众，手指停在最关键的一行
scene: 会议室的灯暗下来，投影亮起，讲者把第一张图表转向台下，手指停在最关键的一行。Her presentation on water reuse lasted twenty minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 presentation 指「演示、报告」（第 1 个义项：面向听众讲解并展示内容）；句意为她关于水循环利用的演示持续了二十分钟。图中可辨识物件：投影幕、图表、讲台。

derivatives.zh: 由 present 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「演示者；主持人」
由 present 加 -able 构成，义为「拿得出手的；像样的」
由 presentation 加 -al 构成，义为「呈现方式的；与展示有关的」

senses.title: A talk that shows and explains something
senses.definition: a formal talk in which someone shows and explains a subject to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 面向听众展示并讲解某一主题的正式讲话
senses.example: She gave a clear presentation on water reuse.
senses.exampleCN: 她就水的循环利用作了一场清晰的报告。
senses.why: The word is built from a Latin verb meaning to place something before someone, so the earliest image is an object set in front of the eyes, which is exactly what a talk with slides does.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自一个拉丁动词，意思是「把东西放到某人面前」，所以最早的画面是把物件摆到眼前给人看；带幻灯片的报告做的正是这件事，于是「演示」成为最贴近原意的义项。

senses.title: The act of giving something formally
senses.definition: a formal ceremony or act in which something is given to someone
senses.definitionCN: 把某物正式交给某人的仪式或行为
senses.example: The presentation of the prize took place at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 颁奖仪式在中午举行。
senses.why: If presenting is placing something in front of a person, the same gesture covers handing a gift or an award into someone's hands, so the verb of showing becomes a noun of giving.
senses.whyCN: 既然「呈现」是把东西放到人面前，那么把礼物或奖章交到对方手上也是同一个动作，于是表示「展示」的词自然分出「赠予、颁发」这一义。

senses.title: The way something appears or is shown
senses.definition: the way in which something is shown, arranged, or appears to others
senses.definitionCN: 某物被展示、安排或呈现给他人的方式
senses.example: The presentation of the data matters as much as the data.
senses.exampleCN: 数据的呈现方式和数据本身同样重要。
senses.why: Once the word names the act of putting something before the eyes, it can also name the resulting look, because what the audience sees is the arrangement itself.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词指「把东西摆到眼前」这个动作，它也能指摆好之后的样子，因为观众看到的正是那个安排方式，所以词义从「动作」滑到「呈现出来的形态」。

senses.title: A first public performance
senses.definition: the first public performance of a play, film, or piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧、电影或音乐作品首次公开演出
senses.example: The new opera had its presentation in Vienna.
senses.exampleCN: 这部新歌剧在维也纳首演。
senses.why: A performance puts a work before an audience for the first time, which is the same placing-before gesture, so the word extends from showing an object to showing a whole work.
senses.whyCN: 演出就是把一部作品第一次摆到观众面前，仍是「置于人前」的手势，所以词义从展示一件物品扩展到展示一整部作品，专指首演。

intro.en: Presentation comes from a Latin verb for placing something before someone; the noun names that placing, and English spread it from showing to giving and performing.
intro.cn: presentation 来自表示「把东西放到某人面前」的拉丁动词；名词指这一摆放动作，英语再把它从展示扩展到赠予与演出。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front, and it marks whatever is set ahead of something else.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前、在前面」，标示被放在别的东西之前。

items.en: The verb esse meant to be, and its present participle praesens described what is here and in front of someone.
items.cn: 动词 esse 意为「存在、是」，它的现在分词 praesens 指「在场的、在某人面前的」。

items.en: Praesentare turned that adjective into a verb: to bring something into someone's presence, to place it before the eyes.
items.cn: praesentare 把这个形容词变成动词：把东西带到某人面前，摆到眼前。

items.en: The noun praesentatio named the act of placing or showing, and it passed into Old French as presentation with the same sense.
items.cn: 名词 praesentatio 指「摆放、展示」这一行为，进入古法语后写作 presentation，含义不变。

items.en: English took the French noun as presentation and widened it to talks, awards, visible forms, and first performances.
items.cn: 英语从法语借入 presentation，并把词义扩展到报告、颁奖、呈现形态与首演。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin adjective for being present and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers other kinds of public talk and display.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示「在场」的拉丁形容词及其英语词族展开；近义组收其他公开讲话与陈列展示的说法。

entries.definition: The verb and adjective at the base of presentation: to show or give, or being in a place.
entries.definitionCN: presentation 的动词与形容词基础形式：展示、赠送，或「在场的」。

entries.definition: The state of being in a place or near someone.
entries.definitionCN: 在场；存在；出席。

entries.definition: A person who gives a presentation or hosts a show.
entries.definitionCN: 作演示的人；节目主持人。

entries.definition: Tidy enough to be shown or offered to others.
entries.definitionCN: 拿得出手的；像样的。

entries.definition: A formal talk given to an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 面向听众的正式讲话。

entries.definition: An educational talk, usually to students.
entries.definitionCN: 通常面向学生的教学讲座。

entries.definition: A practical showing of how something works.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物如何运作的示范。

entries.definition: An arrangement of things put out for people to see.
entries.definitionCN: 把物品摆出来供人观看的陈列。

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin act of placing something before someone, dressed with an English noun ending; its family returns again and again to showing and handing over.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「把东西放到人前」的动作，加上英语名词后缀；同族词反复回到展示与交出。

normal.en: Presentation is present plus -ation: present means placing something before someone, and -ation names the act, so the word is literally the act of placing before.
normal.cn: presentation 是 present 加 -ation：present 指把东西放到人面前，-ation 命名这个动作，所以字面就是「摆到人前」这件事。

normal.en: Presenter swaps -ation for -er, turning the act into the person who performs it.
normal.cn: presenter 把 -ation 换成 -er，把动作变成做这个动作的人。

normal.en: Presentable keeps the -able ending: something that can be presented, that is fit to be shown.
normal.cn: presentable 保留 -able，表示「可以被呈现的」，也就是拿得出手的。

normal.en: Presence and presentation share the same Latin adjective praesens, which describes what is here in front of you.
normal.cn: presence 与 presentation 共用同一个拉丁形容词 praesens，都描述「就在你眼前」的东西。

normal.en: The award sense survives in phrases like the presentation of prizes, where the act of handing over is still a public placing before the crowd.
normal.cn: 「颁发」这一义仍活在 the presentation of prizes 一类说法里：把东西交出去，仍是在众人面前的一次公开摆放。

abstract.en: Every presentation moves something invisible, an idea or a claim, into the space in front of other people.
abstract.cn: 每一场演示都把看不见的东西——一个想法或一个主张——搬进别人眼前的空间。

abstract.en: The same word covers a slide talk and a medal ceremony because both put an object where eyes can reach it.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指幻灯片报告又指颁奖，因为两者都是把东西放到目光够得着的地方。

abstract.en: To present is to accept that a thing is judged by how it is placed, not only by what it is.
abstract.cn: 去呈现，就是承认一件事会被按照「摆放的方式」来评判，而不只看它本身是什么。

examples.en: The presentation lasted twenty minutes and ended with questions.
examples.cn: 这场演示持续了二十分钟，最后以提问结束。

examples.en: The presentation of the awards began at noon.
examples.cn: 颁奖仪式在中午开始。

examples.en: His calm presentation of the facts convinced the room.
examples.cn: 他对事实的冷静呈现说服了在场所有人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞森特申」——把东西「送到」大家面前，就是演示与颁发；谐音只帮记忆，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ esse（存在，现在分词 praesens「在场的」）→ praesentare（摆到面前）→ 拉丁名词 praesentatio → 古法语 presentation → 英语 presentation；核心是「把东西置于人前」。

sensesIntro.en: The core act is placing something before someone; the senses divide into a public talk, a formal handover, a visible form, and a first performance.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心动作是「把东西摆到人前」；义项由此分为公开报告、正式交付、可见形态与首次演出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker turning a chart toward the audience and stopping a finger on the key line.
core.cn: 核心意象：讲者把图表转向听众，手指停在最关键的一行。

branches.en: a slide turning toward the audience
branches.cn: 幻灯片转向听众

branches.en: a speaker pausing on the key figure
branches.cn: 讲者在关键数字上停顿

branches.en: a medal placed in a waiting hand
branches.cn: 奖章放进等候的手心

branches.en: the same facts arranged two different ways
branches.cn: 同样的事实被排成两种样子

branches.en: a curtain rising on a first night
branches.cn: 首演之夜拉开的幕布

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin prefix of place, a Latin verb of being, the verb that means to place before, and the noun and English endings built on them.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示位置的拉丁前缀、表示「存在」的拉丁动词、表示「摆到前面」的动词，以及其上的名词与英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: being present, in front of someone
to show or give; a gift

definition_zh: 保存；保护；维持；果酱；自然保护区；专属领域
definition_en: to keep something in its original state, or to protect it from harm or change
core_image: 一排玻璃罐把夏天的果子封在糖水里，罐外的果园已经落光了叶子
scene: 果园早已光秃，玻璃罐却把夏天的收成保存了下来。Glass jars preserve the summer harvest long after the orchard is bare.
sceneCN: 这里 preserve 指「用糖或盐把食物处理过，使其长期不坏」（第 5 个义项：以糖渍、腌渍等方式保存食物）；句意为果园早已光秃，玻璃罐仍封着夏天的收成。图中可辨识物件：玻璃罐、糖汁、果块、贴着手写日期的标签；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 保存；保护；维持；腌制（食物）
蜜饯；果酱（常用复数）；自然保护区；专属领域

derivatives.zh: 保存；保护；维护
防腐剂 / 防腐的
保存者；救生用具
可保存的
文物保护主义者

senses.title: Keep something from decaying
senses.definition: to treat or store something so that it does not decay
senses.definitionCN: 通过处理或存放使某物不腐坏
senses.example: Salt and smoke preserve meat through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 盐与烟熏能让肉在整个冬天不坏。
senses.why: prae- 'before' plus servare 'keep' gives 'keep beforehand', and keeping food before it spoils is the oldest use of the word.
senses.whyCN: prae-「在前」加 servare「守住」得到「提前守住」，在食物变坏之前先护住，正是这个词最古老的用法。

senses.title: Protect a place from destruction
senses.titleCN: 保护地点、建筑不遭破坏或改造
senses.definition: to protect a building, place or object from being destroyed or altered
senses.definitionCN: 保护建筑、地点或物件不被摧毁或改动
senses.example: The trust preserves the medieval bridge exactly as it stands.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托机构让这座中世纪桥原样留存。
senses.why: the object sense keeps the core meaning untouched: what is preserved is not repaired into something new but kept as it was.
senses.whyCN: 物件义保持了核心含义：被 preserve 的不是被修成新东西，而是按原样留住。

senses.title: Keep a state or quality in being
senses.titleCN: 维持某种状态或品质继续存在
senses.definition: to keep a condition, quality or state continuing
senses.definitionCN: 使某种状况、品质或状态持续下去
senses.example: Officers preserved order while the crowd pushed forward.
senses.exampleCN: 人群向前涌时，警员维持着秩序。
senses.why: order is something that disappears unless it is actively kept, so the verb is used for conditions that need guarding.
senses.whyCN: 秩序若不主动守住就会消失，因此这个词也用于需要守护的状态。

senses.title: Keep something for later generations
senses.titleCN: 为后世留存记录或实物
senses.definition: to keep records, objects or knowledge so that people in the future can still use them
senses.definitionCN: 保存记录、实物或知识，使后人仍能使用
senses.example: Archivists preserve recordings of dialects that no longer have young speakers.
senses.exampleCN: 档案人员保存那些已无年轻使用者的方言录音。
senses.why: here the word looks forward: what is kept now is kept for a time the keeper will never see.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词朝向未来：此刻守住的东西，是为守者永远看不到的时代而留。

senses.title: Prepare fruit or meat with sugar or brine
senses.titleCN: 用糖渍、盐腌等方式加工食物
senses.definition: to prepare fruit or other food with sugar, salt or vinegar so that it keeps
senses.definitionCN: 用糖、盐或醋处理水果等食物以延长保存期
senses.example: Glass jars preserve the summer harvest long after the orchard is bare.
senses.exampleCN: 果园早已光秃，玻璃罐仍封着夏天的收成。
senses.why: the cooking sense specializes the general one: sugar and salt are the agents that do the guarding.
senses.whyCN: 烹调用法是一般义的具体化：糖与盐就是执行「守住」的媒介。

senses.title: A protected area of land
senses.definition: an area of land set aside so that its wildlife or landscape is protected
senses.definitionCN: 为保护野生生物或景观而划出的土地
senses.example: The marsh is a private preserve where hunting is banned.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沼泽是私人保护区，禁止狩猎。
senses.why: the noun turns the act into a place: land where protection happens all the time.
senses.whyCN: 名词义把动作变成地点：持续进行保护的那片土地。

senses.title: Fruit jam in a jar
senses.titleCN: 果酱、蜜饯（美式常用复数）
senses.definition: fruit cooked with sugar and stored in jars
senses.definitionCN: 加糖熬煮后装罐的水果制品
senses.example: She opened a jar of strawberry preserves for the toast.
senses.exampleCN: 她开了一罐草莓酱配吐司。
senses.why: the product noun is inherited straight from the verb, and American English prefers the plural for the jars on the shelf.
senses.whyCN: 成品名词直接承自动词，美式英语更常用复数指架上的那些罐子。

senses.title: An activity reserved for one group
senses.titleCN: 某一群体独占的领域或活动
senses.definition: an activity or area that one group keeps for itself and others are shut out of
senses.definitionCN: 某一群体留给自己、他人不得进入的活动或领域
senses.example: Editing the paper is no longer a male preserve.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑这家报纸不再是男性的专属领域。
senses.why: the idea of keeping something safe for oneself shades easily into keeping others out, which is how this social sense arose.
senses.whyCN: 把某物为自己守住，很容易滑向把别人挡在外面，这个社会义就是这样产生的。

intro.en: Preserve comes through Old French from Latin praeservare, built on prae- 'before' and servare 'to keep'. It shares its root with conserve but not its prefix. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: preserve 经古法语来自拉丁 praeservare，由 prae-「在前」与 servare「守住」构成。它与 conserve 共享词根，但前缀不同。年代均为约数。

items.en: Prae- meant 'before, in front of', and in compounds it often adds the idea of doing something in advance.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在……之前」，在复合词中常添「预先」的意思。

items.en: Praeservare meant 'to keep or guard beforehand', a combination of the prefix with servare 'to keep safe'.
items.cn: praeservare 意为「提前看守、预先保住」，是前缀与 servare「守住」的组合。

items.en: Old French preserver brought the word into English in the fourteenth century, and the spelling settled as preserve.
items.cn: 古法语 preserver 在 14 世纪把词带入英语，拼写最终固定为 preserve。

items.en: The food sense is recorded from the sixteenth century; the sense of land set aside for wildlife developed in the nineteenth, when the first large reserves were mapped.
items.cn: 食物义在 16 世纪有记录；为野生生物划出土地的意思在 19 世纪形成，当时最早的几处大型保护区被勘定。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest citation for the jam noun and for the nature-reserve sense is not precisely recorded, and the pre-Latin origin of servare remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：果酱名词义与自然保护区义的最早书证没有确切记录；servare 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds verbs that share the Latin -serve stock and are easily mistaken; group two holds words that also mean keeping something safe but differ in emphasis.
note.cn: 第一组是共享拉丁 -serve 词干、容易认错的动词；第二组同样表示「保住」，但侧重点不同。

entries.definition: Com- plus servare stresses keeping a resource from being used up; preserve stresses keeping something from changing or spoiling.
entries.definitionCN: com- 加 servare 强调不让资源被用尽；preserve 强调不让某物改变或变坏。

entries.definition: Re- 'back' plus servare: to set something aside instead of using it now, as in reserve a table.
entries.definitionCN: re-「向后」加 servare：把某物留到以后再用，如预订餐桌。

entries.definition: Ob- 'toward' plus servare: to watch, notice, or follow a rule; nothing is being stored.
entries.definitionCN: ob-「朝向」加 servare：观看、察觉或遵守规则；并不涉及储存。

entries.definition: De- 'fully' plus servire 'to serve': to have earned something. Same look, different root.
entries.definitionCN: de-「完全」加 servire「服侍」：因服务而应得。形似而词根不同。

entries.definition: To keep something safe from active harm; it says nothing about keeping it unchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物免受主动伤害；不涉及保持原样。

entries.definition: To keep something one already has, such as heat or a right, without the idea of guarding it.
entries.definitionCN: 指继续保有已拥有之物，如热量或权利，不含守护之意。

entries.definition: To use a resource sparingly so that it lasts; its focus is quantity, not condition.
entries.definitionCN: 节制使用资源使其持久；关注的是数量而非状态。

entries.definition: To keep something working by servicing it, as a machine; preserve does not imply repair.
entries.definitionCN: 通过保养使某物继续运转，如机器；preserve 不含修理之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: prae- 'before' + servare 'keep': guard it before harm arrives.
normal.cn: prae-「在前」+ servare「守住」：在伤害到来之前先护住。

normal.en: The family runs preserve, preservation, preservative, preserver, preservationist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 preserve、preservation、preservative、preserver、preservationist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: preserve food, preserve order, nature preserve, fruit preserves.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：保存食物、维持秩序、自然保护区、果酱。

normal.en: The root is shared with conserve and reserve, but the prefixes do the dividing.
normal.cn: 词根与 conserve、reserve 共享，靠前缀区分。

normal.en: American English says preserves for jam, British English often says jam.
normal.cn: 美式英语用 preserves 指果酱，英式英语常用 jam。

abstract.en: Picture a jar of summer standing on a shelf in January.
abstract.cn: 想象一月的架子上摆着一罐夏天。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge left exactly as it was, weeds and all.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥连杂草都原样留着。

abstract.en: Picture a fence that keeps a meadow for animals and people out of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一道篱笆把草场留给动物，把人挡在外面。

examples.en: The museum preserves the letters in acid-free boxes.
examples.cn: 博物馆把信件放在无酸盒中保存。

examples.en: Freezing preserves the flavour far better than drying.
examples.cn: 冷冻保存风味远胜于干燥。

examples.en: The old quarter is preserved as a living neighbourhood, not a museum.
examples.cn: 这片老城区是作为活着的社区被保护，而不是当成博物馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pre（提前）+ serve（守住）」——在坏掉之前先护住 → 保存、保护、维持

root: 拉丁 praeservare「提前守住」= prae-（在前）+ servare「看守、保存」；与 conserve 共享 servare 词根，靠前缀区分。英语 preserve。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: something is guarded before harm reaches it, and that guard is then applied to food, buildings, order, records, land, jam and finally to a social boundary.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：在损害到达之前先护住某物，这道防护再依次用于食物、建筑、秩序、记录、土地、果酱，最后用于一条社会边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a jar and a fence, both keeping something whole against time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只罐与一道篱笆，都在对抗时间地把某物完整留住。

branches.en: STOP DECAY: sugar, salt and smoke are the guard, whether in a pot or a jar.
branches.cn: 止住腐坏：糖、盐与烟就是那道防护，无论在锅里还是罐里。

branches.en: UNCHANGED OBJECT: a building is kept as it stands, not restored into something new.
branches.cn: 原样的物件：建筑按现状留住，而不是修成新东西。

branches.en: STATE AND RECORD: order and archives both vanish unless someone keeps them.
branches.cn: 状态与记录：秩序与档案若无人守护都会消失。

branches.en: SET ASIDE: the act becomes a place, and the product becomes a jar.
branches.cn: 留出：动作变成一片地，成品变成一罐酱。

branches.en: KEPT FOR SOME: guarding something for oneself ends by shutting others out.
branches.cn: 为某些人留住：为自己守住，最终把别人挡在外面。

intro.en: Preserve is a Latin verb of prefix plus root; the same two parts build conserve, reserve and observe, so the family is best read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: preserve 是由前缀加词根构成的拉丁动词；同样的两部分也构成 conserve、reserve 与 observe，因此这个词族最好按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- 'before' and servare 'to keep' give praeservare; English draws preserve, preservation, preservative and preserver from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 prae-「在前」与 servare「守住」构成 praeservare；英语由此得到 preserve、preservation、preservative 与 preserver。

items.example: The prefix marks action taken ahead of time.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记提前采取的行动。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of guarding.
Salt preserves the fish before it spoils.
items.exampleCN: 盐在鱼变坏之前先把它保住。

items.example: Cold storage aids the preservation of vaccines.
items.exampleCN: 冷藏有助于疫苗的保存。

items.meaning: a substance that keeps food from spoiling
items.meaningCN: 防止食物变坏的添加物
items.exampleCN: 标签上未列出任何防腐剂。

definition_en: the head of a state, a university, a company, or a meeting, especially one chosen to lead and to preside over others
core_image: 一张长桌的尽头，一个人坐在最前面的椅子上，所有人的目光都朝他那边
scene: 长桌两侧坐满了人，争论停不下来，最后大家都看向尽头那把椅子，等坐在那里的人开口。The president of the club called for a vote.
sceneCN: 这里 president 指「会长、会议主席」（第 4 个义项：被推举出来主持会议的人）；句意为俱乐部会长要求进行表决。图中可辨识物件：长桌、成排的椅子、举起的手。

senses.title: The head of a state
senses.definition: the elected head of a republic, who leads the government and represents the country
senses.definitionCN: 共和国的民选元首，领导政府并代表国家
senses.example: The president addressed the nation on television.
senses.exampleCN: 总统通过电视向全国发表讲话。
senses.why: The Latin source means to sit in front, and the leader of a state is pictured as the person seated at the head of the table where decisions are made.
senses.whyCN: 词源本义是「坐在前面」，国家领导人正被想象成长桌首位上坐着的人，所有决定都从他那里发出，因此「总统」是这个坐前意象在政治上的放大。

senses.title: The head of a university
senses.definition: the senior officer who leads a university or a college
senses.definitionCN: 领导一所大学或学院的最高负责人
senses.example: The president welcomed the new students at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 校长在校门口迎接新生。
senses.why: A university is also a body with a council and a hall, so its leader inherits the same image of the person who sits before the assembly and speaks for it.
senses.whyCN: 大学同样有校务会议与礼堂，它的负责人也就继承了同一幅画面：坐在众人之前、代表整个机构讲话的人，于是这个词从国家元首平移到校长。

senses.title: The head of a company
senses.definition: the most senior officer of a company or organization
senses.definitionCN: 公司或机构中职位最高的负责人
senses.example: The president of the firm signed the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 公司董事长签署了这份合同。
senses.why: Boards meet around a table, and the officer who sits at its head and signs for the company keeps the literal seating arrangement inside the modern title.
senses.whyCN: 董事会围桌而坐，坐在首位、代表公司签字的那个人，把「坐前排」的字面安排原样保留在现代头衔里，因此同一个词也指董事长、总裁。

senses.title: The person who chairs a meeting
senses.definition: the person chosen to lead a meeting, a club, or an assembly
senses.definitionCN: 被推选出来主持聚会、俱乐部或集会的负责人
senses.example: The president of the club called for a vote.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部会长要求进行表决。
senses.why: This is the plainest surviving sense: the one who sits in front of the group, keeps order, and lets others speak in turn.
senses.whyCN: 这是最贴近字面的一个义项：坐在一群人前面、维持秩序、安排轮流发言的人；规模没有国家或公司那么大，却仍是「坐前排」的原样动作。

intro.en: President goes back to a Latin verb made of a prefix meaning in front and a verb meaning to sit; the title first named anyone who sat before a group, then the head of a state.
intro.cn: president 可追到由「在前」的前缀与「坐」的动词组成的拉丁语动词；这个头衔最初指坐在一群人前面的人，后来才指国家元首。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front, and it is the same element seen in many Latin words of rank and place.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前、在前面」，与许多表示位次和位置的拉丁词共用这一成分。

items.en: The verb sedere meant to sit, and it is the source of a wide family of English words about seats, sessions, and settling down.
items.cn: 动词 sedere 意为「坐」，派生出一大批关于座位、会议与安顿下来的英语词。

items.en: Praesidere joined the two: to sit before others, and therefore to watch over, guard, or lead an assembly.
items.cn: praesidere 把两者合起来：坐在别人前面，因此引申为看守、护卫、主持一个集会。

items.en: The present participle praesidens, with the stem praesident-, named the person who sits in front; this is the form English took.
items.cn: 现在分词 praesidens 的词干是 praesident-，指坐在前面的人，英语取用的正是这一形式。

items.en: Old French president passed the title into English, first for the officer of a meeting or a college, later for the head of a state and of a company.
items.cn: 古法语 president 把这个头衔传入英语，先指会议或学院的负责人，后来才指国家元首与公司最高负责人。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb for sitting in front; the near-meaning group gathers other titles for the person who leads a body.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示「坐在前面」的拉丁动词展开；近义组收其他称呼团体领导者的头衔。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin phrase turned into a title: the one who sits in front. Every sense keeps that seat at the head of the table.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把一个拉丁短语变成头衔：「坐在前面的人」；每个义项都保留着长桌首位那把椅子。

normal.en: President is prae- plus sedere: the one who sits in front of the others.
normal.cn: president 是 prae- 加 sedere：坐在其他人前面的那个人。

normal.en: Preside is the verb underneath the title, and presidency names the office or the term.
normal.cn: preside 是头衔底下的动词，presidency 则指职位或任期。

normal.en: Presidential adds -ial to make the adjective, as in a presidential election.
normal.cn: presidential 加 -ial 构成形容词，例如 a presidential election（总统选举）。

normal.en: The same Latin verb gave presidium, a standing committee that also sits in front of a larger body.
normal.cn: 同一个拉丁动词也生出 presidium，指同样坐在更大机构前面的常设委员会。

normal.en: A club president and a company president share the title because both chair a body, not because both lead a country.
normal.cn: 俱乐部会长与公司董事长共用一个头衔，是因为两人都在主持一个团体，而不是因为两人都领导国家。

abstract.en: The oldest meaning is a seating plan: the person in the front chair gets to speak for everyone behind.
abstract.cn: 最古老的含义其实是一张座次表：坐在前面椅子上的人，替后面所有人说话。

abstract.en: Power in this word is drawn as a place at the table, which is why the same title fits a state, a school, and a firm.
abstract.cn: 这个词里的权力被画成「桌边的一个位置」，所以同一个头衔能装下国家、学校与公司。

abstract.en: Whenever a group needs one voice, it looks for someone to sit at the head of the table.
abstract.cn: 只要一个群体需要统一的声音，就会找一个人坐到长桌首位。

examples.en: The president addressed the nation on television.
examples.cn: 总统通过电视向全国发表讲话。

examples.en: The president of the university opened the ceremony.
examples.cn: 大学校长宣布典礼开始。

examples.en: She was elected president of the student union.
examples.cn: 她当选为学生会主席。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞兹登特」——坐在最前面的人（pre- 在前，sid 坐），就是主席与总统；谐音只助记。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ sedere（坐）→ praesidere（坐在前面、主持）→ 现在分词 praesidens（坐在前面的人）→ 古法语 president → 英语 president；字面就是「坐前排的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the seat at the front; the senses spread from chairing a small meeting to leading a university, a company, and a state.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「前排的座位」；义项从主持小会议，扩展到领导大学、公司与国家。

core.cn: 核心意象：一张长桌，尽头一把椅子，所有面孔都朝那边。
